Bringing written material into the testing room violates the testing rules whether or not the candidate reads it, because what is compromised is the security and integrity of the exam itself; the violation of Standard VII(A) is complete once the material is carried in.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(A), a candidate who objects to a proctor's instruction at the test center is most likely:

options.A: obliged to comply with the instruction.
options.B: entitled to decline a check she considers intrusive.
options.C: answerable to local law rather than to the Standard.

rationales.A: Candidates must comply with proctor instructions and with the testing rules. Refusing to cooperate, becoming agitated, shouting profanity, or threatening a proctor violates Standard VII(A), because such conduct violates the testing rules and compromises the integrity and security of the CFA exam. Conduct must remain professional throughout the testing process, including check-in and security screening.
rationales.B: A candidate's own view of how intrusive a check is creates no right to refuse it. Declining a proctor's security procedure still violates the testing rules and compromises the integrity and security of the exam, and so violates Standard VII(A).
rationales.C: Conduct at the test center falls squarely within Standard VII(A), not merely within local law. The Standard reaches any conduct that compromises the integrity, validity, or security of CFA Institute programs, so a dispute with a proctor is judged against it whatever the applicable local law provides.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(A), a member who grades CFA exams is most likely:

options.A: free to discuss the materials once scores are released.
options.B: bound as to scoring rubrics but not as to questions.
options.C: free to discuss the exam only with staff and fellow graders.

rationales.A: The grader's undertaking bars discussion with anyone other than CFA Institute staff and fellow graders, and the release of scores changes nothing. Question content, guideline answers, scoring results by question, and grading deliberations remain confidential after results are published.
rationales.B: The undertaking covers the exam materials broadly, the questions included, not merely the scoring rubrics. Specific questions, the guideline answer, scoring results by question, and the deliberations related to grading all sit within the grader's confidentiality obligation.
rationales.C: As a condition of participating in grading CFA exams, a grader agrees not to reveal or discuss the exam materials with anyone except CFA Institute staff or other graders. That undertaking covers information related to specific questions on the exam, the guideline answer, scoring results by question, and deliberations related to grading. A grader who disclosed information about a specific exam question violated Standard VII(A), because the disclosure compromised the integrity of the exam process.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(A), a candidate posting in a public online forum after sitting the exam is most likely:

options.A: barred from any discussion of the exam whatsoever.
options.B: barred from discussing specific exam content only.
options.C: barred from discussing content until the next sitting.

rationales.A: General impressions are not confidential. Writing about how difficult the candidate found the exam, or about how well she thinks she performed, does not violate Standard VII(A); only disclosure of specific content does. A blanket prohibition on all post-exam discussion therefore overstates the obligation.
rationales.B: Post-exam discussion of the exam's general difficulty and of the candidate's own performance is permitted. What Standard VII(A) prohibits is discussion of specific content: topics covered and not covered, formulas tested and not tested, question-specific details, and attempts to work out the correct answers. A candidate who wrote about how difficult she found the exam and how well she thought she had done did not violate the Standard, but she did violate it by revealing which areas the exam covered and which it did not. A study group that pooled question-specific details in order to determine correct answers also violated it. Candidates should stay out of threads that attempt to reconstruct exam content.
rationales.C: Question-specific confidentiality does not lapse when the next sitting comes round. Exam information stays confidential until CFA Institute itself releases it publicly, so a later exam cycle does not free the prior window's question content for discussion.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(A), a candidate asked by a test-prep provider to describe exam questions is most likely:

options.A: obliged to refuse the provider's request.
options.B: entitled to share recollections with the provider.
options.C: obliged to refuse only a request that offers payment.

rationales.A: Candidates and members should refuse to share exam content with test-prep providers or any other third party, even when they are solicited for it. Providing exam questions or content undermines the integrity of the exam, and the information remains confidential until CFA Institute releases it publicly. A candidate who disclosed exam questions to a prep provider violated Standard VII(A); and if the provider's employees who solicited the information are themselves CFA Institute members or candidates, they violated the Standard as well by seeking confidential information.
rationales.B: Exam content is confidential and the motive for sharing it is irrelevant. Supplying recollected questions or content to a prep provider compromises the integrity of the exam process and violates Standard VII(A), however much it might improve candidates' preparation.
rationales.C: The duty to refuse applies whether or not compensation is offered. The violation lies in disclosing confidential exam content, not in being paid for it, so an uncompensated disclosure to a prep provider breaches Standard VII(A) exactly as a paid one does.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(A), a candidate's duty to be truthful in dealings with CFA Institute is most likely:

options.A: limited to exam answers and not to deferral filings.
options.B: of no professional consequence absent a client.
options.C: broad enough to reach a fraudulent deferral request.

rationales.A: The duty is not confined to exam answers. Administrative submissions to CFA Institute, including deferral requests, registration information, and supporting documentation, must be truthful, and a misrepresentation in any of them violates Standard VII(A).
rationales.B: The absence of a client relationship is irrelevant. Standard VII(A) reaches conduct that compromises the integrity, validity, or security of CFA Institute programs, so a fraudulent representation made to the Institute about one of its programs violates the Standard directly, and the knowing misstatement violates Standard I(C) Misrepresentation as well.
rationales.C: Misrepresenting information to CFA Institute regarding any CFA Institute program violates Standard VII(A). Filing a fraudulent emergency deferral request supported by altered documentation breaks the rules of the CFA Program and compromises the integrity of the exam, so it violates Standard VII(A), and because it is a knowing misstatement it violates Standard I(C) Misrepresentation in addition. Candidates must be truthful in all communications and filings with CFA Institute, not only in their exam answers.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(A), use of an association with CFA Institute to advance personal or professional goals is most likely:

options.A: open to volunteers for client development.
options.B: prohibited as improper use of the association.
options.C: restricted to the Institute's paid staff alone.

rationales.A: Volunteering earns no such privilege. Improperly using an association with CFA Institute to achieve personal or professional goals is prohibited conduct under Standard VII(A), and turning a volunteer post into client development is the clearest form of it.
rationales.B: Members and candidates must not improperly use an association with CFA Institute to achieve personal or professional goals. A volunteer who scheduled only his own clients to speak at society events, or who otherwise leveraged a volunteer role for personal gain, compromises the reputation and integrity of CFA Institute and so violates Standard VII(A). Membership, the charter, and a volunteer position may be referred to factually, but they may not be converted into a marketing advantage.
rationales.C: The prohibition is not limited to paid CFA Institute staff. Volunteers, such as society directors, committee members, and exam graders, are the guidance's principal examples, precisely because their roles carry the association with CFA Institute that may not be exploited.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(A), a member's expression of disagreement with CFA Institute policies is most likely:

options.A: permitted only through official feedback channels.
options.B: permitted in any forum short of exam content.
options.C: prohibited while the member holds the charter.

rationales.A: No channel restriction exists. Opinions about CFA Institute and its programs may be voiced publicly and in any forum, not only through official feedback channels. The boundary Standard VII(A) draws is around confidential exam content, not around where an opinion is expressed.
rationales.B: Standard VII(A) does not cover the expression of opinions regarding CFA Institute or its programs. Members and candidates are free to disagree, and to express their disagreement, with CFA Institute's policies, its procedures, or any advocacy position the organization takes. What remains prohibited when such an opinion is expressed is the disclosure of confidential information about exam content, including any actual exam questions and information about subject matter covered or not covered on an exam. The freedom to opine does not extend to confidential specifics.
rationales.C: Holding the charter does not silence disagreement. Members may publicly disagree with CFA Institute policies, procedures, and advocacy positions, and may argue for changing them; only the disclosure of confidential program content, such as exam questions or the subject matter covered, is barred.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(A), the program rules and policies posted by CFA Institute are most likely:

options.A: non-binding drafts of policy yet to take effect.
options.B: binding definitions of allowed and disallowed conduct.
options.C: reminders binding only once a proctor recites them.

rationales.A: The posted policies are not drafts awaiting effect. They define allowed and disallowed conduct as they stand, and a violation of any of the testing policies constitutes a violation of Standard VII(A).
rationales.B: The rules, regulations, and policies for CFA Institute programs define additional allowed and disallowed actions concerning the programs and the examinations, and violating any of the testing policies is itself a violation of Standard VII(A). Those policies are posted on the CFA Institute website, and members and candidates are expected to be aware of them and to comply with them.
rationales.C: Accountability does not depend on what a proctor says aloud. The programs' posted rules, regulations, and policies bind every participant, and members and candidates are expected to know them and comply with them before exam day.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(A), the prohibition on disregarding or circumventing examination security measures is most likely:

options.A: subject to a de minimis exception.
options.B: directed at test centers rather than candidates.
options.C: triggered by the attempt alone.

rationales.A: Standard VII(A) names disregarding or attempting to circumvent security measures established for any CFA Institute examinations as prohibited conduct, and it attaches no de minimis threshold to that prohibition. A workaround the candidate considers minor, such as bringing an unauthorized calculator model into the test center, is still the disregard of a security measure established for the examination, so it falls squarely within the prohibition rather than below the standard's concern.
rationales.B: The security measures are established for CFA Institute examinations, but the conduct standard binds the members and candidates subject to it, not the test centers that administer it. A candidate who works around a security control is the violator under VII(A); the administrative obligations of the test center are a separate matter and do not displace the candidate's own duty.
rationales.C: One of the categories of prohibited conduct under Standard VII(A) is disregarding or attempting to circumvent security measures established for any CFA Institute examinations. The guidance states that prohibited conduct includes, but is not limited to, disregarding or attempting to circumvent security measures established for any CFA Institute examinations. Two features of that language matter. The prohibition covers both explicit rule violations and efforts to work around security controls, and it reaches the attempt itself, so a candidate violates the standard whether or not the circumvention succeeds.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(A), the prohibition on giving or receiving assistance on an examination is most likely:

options.A: conditional on the candidate having solicited it.
options.B: directed at the provider of the help.
options.C: applied to the provider and the recipient alike.

rationales.A: Standard VII(A) prohibits giving or receiving assistance, that is, cheating, on any CFA Institute examinations, and nothing in the prohibition turns on who initiated the exchange. Accepting assistance is prohibited whether or not the candidate solicited it, because the integrity and validity of the examination are compromised either way.
rationales.B: The standard reaches both sides of the exchange. Prohibited conduct includes giving or receiving assistance, so the candidate who provides examination content and the candidates who accept it all violate Standard VII(A). A recipient who solicits and accepts examination information compromises the integrity and validity of that exam just as the provider does, and so is equally in breach.
rationales.C: Prohibited conduct under Standard VII(A) includes giving or receiving assistance, that is, cheating, on any CFA Institute examinations. Both the provider and the recipient of assistance violate the standard: a candidate who passes examination content to others is in breach, and the candidates who solicit and accept that information are equally in breach, because by doing so they compromise the integrity and validity of the examination. The guidance also frames its list of prohibited conduct as illustrative rather than exhaustive, so conduct of the same character is caught even where it is not spelled out.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(A), CFA Institute's response to online material that breaches examination rules is most likely:

options.A: removal of the material in an annual review.
options.B: tolerance of the material once posted.
options.C: prompt removal of the material.

rationales.A: The response is prompt rather than periodic. The guidance states that the organization works to promptly address or remove any and all material that violates exam or other rules, laws, or regulations, so action is continuous and taken as the material is found; it is not held back for an annual review or a periodic sanctioning exercise.
rationales.B: Material posted in online forums is within the organization's reach and is not tolerated. CFA Institute works to promptly address or remove any and all material that violates exam or other rules, laws, or regulations, and that includes content posted to discussion forums and social platforms.
rationales.C: The organization works to promptly address or remove any and all material that violates exam or other rules, laws, or regulations. For members and candidates the practical consequence is twofold. Content that breaches examination confidentiality will be actively pursued and taken down, and they should not take part in such disclosure even in forums that look ephemeral or anonymous, because participation is itself prohibited conduct under Standard VII(A).

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(B), a member's recommended handling of written information about the standard and its guidance is most likely:

options.A: a copy to legal, compliance, public relations, and marketing.
options.B: a copy to the marketing department.
options.C: retention for the member's own reference.

rationales.A: Members and candidates should disseminate written information about Standard VII(B) and the accompanying guidance to their firm's legal, compliance, public relations, and marketing departments. All four of those groups draft or vet materials that may reference CFA Institute membership, the CFA designation, or candidacy for the designation, so circulating the guidance to each of them is what keeps the firm's references aligned with the standard.
rationales.B: Marketing is only one of the four departments named in the recommended practice. The guidance also reaches legal, compliance, and public relations, because each of those groups likewise produces or reviews materials that may refer to CFA Institute membership, the designation, or candidacy.
rationales.C: The guidance is not for the member's personal reference alone. The recommended compliance practice is to disseminate written information about Standard VII(B) and the accompanying guidance to the firm's legal, compliance, public relations, and marketing departments, precisely so that the people drafting firm materials know what the standard requires.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(B), firm templates for materials referring to employees' CFA Institute affiliation are most likely:

options.A: discouraged as a constraint on expression.
options.B: encouraged for consistency with the standard.
options.C: subject to CFA Institute pre-approval.

rationales.A: Templates are encouraged, not discouraged. Members and candidates should encourage their firms to create templates consistent with Standard VII(B) for materials that refer to employees' affiliation with CFA Institute. The point of a template is to prevent inadvertent misuse, and the interest in consistent, accurate references outweighs any loss of individual phrasing.
rationales.B: For materials that refer to employees' affiliation with CFA Institute, members and candidates should encourage their firms to create templates that are consistent with Standard VII(B). The guidance states the purpose of that practice: it promotes consistent and accurate references to CFA Institute membership, the CFA designation, and candidacy for the CFA designation. Consistency is the mechanism, because a vetted template removes the chance that each author improvises a different and possibly misleading description.
rationales.C: No pre-approval process applies. Firms adopt templates themselves, consistent with the published guidance on Standard VII(B); CFA Institute does not review or clear firm materials before they are used, so responsibility for accuracy stays with the member, the candidate, and the firm.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(B), a charterholder's statement of charterholder status is most likely:

options.A: accurate and free of exaggeration.
options.B: understated to avoid the look of promotion.
options.C: open to overstatement in competitive marketing.

rationales.A: Charterholders are encouraged to use the designation but, in doing so, must state their charterholder status in a manner that is accurate and does not exaggerate the benefits of the charter. The guidance adds that use of the designation may be accompanied by an accurate explanation of the requirements that have been met to earn the right to use it, so an explanatory statement is permitted as long as it stays factual.
rationales.B: Use of the designation is encouraged, so holding back references is not what the standard asks for. The requirement is accuracy: state charterholder status in a manner that does not exaggerate the benefits of the charter, and, where the reference is explained, explain accurately the requirements that have been met to earn the right to use the designation.
rationales.C: There is no marketing tolerance for exaggeration. References must be accurate and must not exaggerate the benefits of the charter, whatever the competitive setting, so a claim that overstates what the charter signifies breaches Standard VII(B) even when the overstatement is a modest one.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(B), a charterholder's continued right to use the designation most likely rests on:

options.A: a filing made in the year the charter is awarded.
options.B: payment of dues each year.
options.C: satisfaction of the annual membership requirements.

rationales.A: The annual membership requirements are ongoing, not a formality discharged once in the year the charter is awarded. Having been granted the right to use the designation, the individual must satisfy CFA Institute annual membership requirements each year to maintain that right, and failure to meet any one of them forfeits the right until membership is reestablished.
rationales.B: Dues alone are not enough. Annual membership requires completing a Membership Agreement, submitting the Professional Conduct Statement, and paying dues. All three components must be satisfied, and failing any single one costs the individual the right to use the designation.
rationales.C: Individuals must satisfy CFA Institute annual membership requirements, namely completing a Membership Agreement, submitting the Professional Conduct Statement, and paying dues, in order to maintain their right to use the CFA designation. The guidance is explicit that once granted the right to use the designation, individuals must also satisfy CFA Institute annual membership requirements to maintain that right, and that a charterholder who fails to meet any membership requirement forfeits the right to use the CFA designation until membership is reestablished.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(B), CFA Institute membership and holding the CFA designation are most likely:

options.A: a single status conferred together.
options.B: separate statuses under the standard.
options.C: independent once the charter is awarded.

rationales.A: This conflates two separate things. CFA Institute membership requires an annual Membership Agreement, a Professional Conduct Statement, and payment of dues, while the designation is earned separately by satisfying the CFA Program requirements and receiving Board approval. Membership requires annual renewal; the designation is awarded once, on different conditions, so passing the examinations does not by itself confer both as one status.
rationales.B: CFA Institute membership and holding the CFA designation are separate statuses under Standard VII(B). Membership requires an annual Membership Agreement, a Professional Conduct Statement filing, and payment of dues. The designation is earned separately, after the CFA Program requirements are satisfied and the Board approves the award. The two interlock in one direction only: use of the designation is governed by the terms and conditions of the CFA Institute Membership Agreement and applicable law, so a charterholder must also satisfy the annual membership requirements in order to maintain the right to use the designation.
rationales.C: The two do not become independent when the charter is awarded, and holding the charter exempts no one from the membership requirements. Once granted the right to use the designation, individuals must also satisfy CFA Institute annual membership requirements to maintain that right, and a charterholder who fails any membership requirement forfeits the right to use the designation.

questions.stem: A candidate who declines to sit for an examination for which they enrolled is most likely:

options.A: barred from candidacy thereafter.
options.B: a candidate still, through the skipped sitting.
options.C: no longer a candidate until enrolled again.

rationales.A: The lapse is not permanent. An individual who declines to sit ceases to be a candidate, but once that person is enrolled to sit for a future examination, his or her candidacy resumes. Nothing in the guidance bars the individual from referring to candidacy again after re-enrolling.
rationales.B: Candidacy does not carry through a skipped examination. If an individual declines to sit for an exam for which they have enrolled, or otherwise does not meet the definition of a candidate as described in the CFA Institute Bylaws, that individual is no longer considered a candidate. Fees paid for an earlier sitting do not keep the status alive in the interval before the person re-enrolls.
rationales.C: If an individual declines to sit for an exam for which they have enrolled or otherwise does not meet the definition of a candidate as described in the CFA Institute Bylaws, then that individual is no longer considered a candidate. The status is suspended rather than ended: once the person is enrolled to sit for a future examination, his or her candidacy resumes. The practical consequence is that references to being a CFA Program candidate must stop during the gap and may be made again only after enrollment for a future exam.

questions.stem: Until membership is reestablished, a lapsed member's references to the CFA designation are most likely:

options.A: retained until reinstatement completes.
options.B: removed wherever they appear.
options.C: corrected in new materials going forward.

rationales.A: Use must stop on lapse, not when reinstatement completes. Until membership is reestablished, individuals must not present themselves to others as CFA charterholders, so pending paperwork confers no interim right to use the designation; the right returns only once membership is actually reestablished.
rationales.B: Until membership is reestablished, individuals must not present themselves to others as CFA charterholders and must remove all references to the CFA designation from social media profiles, business communications, reports, and anywhere else the designation is referenced. One thing remains permissible: former members may state that they were charterholders in the past, provided the statement is accurate and framed in the past tense.
rationales.C: The obligation is not limited to newly produced materials. All references must be removed wherever the designation appears, including social media profiles, business communications, reports, and anywhere else it is referenced, so existing biographies have to be corrected as well. Only a past-tense statement that the individual was formerly a charterholder may remain.

questions.stem: A member's firm website states that CFA charterholders commit to ethical and professional conduct and that the CFA exams are thorough and rigorous. Under Standard VII(B), the statement is most likely:

options.A: permitted only with pass-rate statistics.
options.B: prohibited as unverifiable puffery.
options.C: appropriate as written.

rationales.A: No statistical-support condition attaches to these statements. The guidance recognizes commitment to ethical and professional conduct, and the thoroughness and rigor of the CFA exams, as proper subjects of reference in their own right, and attaches no requirement of supporting statistics to either.
rationales.B: Statements of this kind are appropriate rather than prohibited. The guidance treats members' commitment to ethical and professional conduct and the rigor of the exams as recognized, proper themes; what Standard VII(B) forbids is misrepresenting the meaning of membership, the designation or candidacy, overstating an individual's competency, or asserting or implying that superior investment performance can be expected from a charterholder. Describing an ethical obligation makes none of those claims.
rationales.C: Statements that highlight or emphasize the commitment of CFA Institute members, CFA charterholders, and CFA candidates to ethical and professional conduct, or that mention the thoroughness and rigor of the CFA exams, are appropriate. They describe the program and the obligations of those who participate in it rather than asserting an investment result, so no supporting statistics are required and no inference of superior performance arises.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(B), a reference to participation in the CFA Program by a Level III candidate on business materials is most likely:

options.A: acceptable in the shorthand form 'CFA III'.
options.B: prohibited until the charter is awarded.
options.C: permitted if it clearly states candidate status.

rationales.A: Credential-style shorthand such as 'CFA III' sets the letters out as though they were a designation already held, which implies a partial designation. There is no partial designation: a reference must clearly state that the individual is a candidate for the CFA designation. 'CFA, Expected 20XX' fails for the same reason and adds a second defect, an implied completion date the candidate cannot promise.
rationales.B: Referencing candidacy is permitted, so silence until the charter is awarded is not required. The requirement is clear, factual framing of the reference, as in 'I am a 20XX Level III candidate for the CFA designation,' which states the candidacy as a candidacy and claims nothing further.
rationales.C: Candidates for the CFA designation may reference their candidacy, but such references must clearly state that the individual is a candidate for the CFA designation. An acceptable format is 'I am a 20XX Level III candidate for the CFA designation.' An unacceptable format is 'CFA, Expected 20XX,' because it implies both a partial designation and an expected completion date.

questions.stem: A member's LinkedIn profile and the professional biography her firm's marketing team maintains for her both refer to her CFA designation. Her references to the designation in these communications are most likely:

options.A: governed by platform norms rather than by Standard VII(B).
options.B: assigned to the firm rather than to the member.
options.C: covered by Standard VII(B) like any other communication.

rationales.A: The standard applies to any form of communication, and the guidance names LinkedIn pages and directory listings expressly among the electronic formats it reaches. A member who does not control a platform's layout still controls the words entered into it, which is what the accuracy requirement governs.
rationales.B: A professional biography is a communication about the member, and the member remains responsible for the accuracy of every reference to CFA Institute membership, the designation or candidacy within it, wherever it is published and whoever typesets it. Firm involvement in producing the document does not displace that personal duty.
rationales.C: Standard VII(B) applies to any form of communication, including but not limited to communications made in electronic or written form such as firm letterhead, business cards, professional biographies, directory listings, printed advertising, LinkedIn pages, email signatures, websites and personal resumes, and to oral statements made to the public, clients or prospects. The same requirements of accuracy and non-exaggeration apply in every channel, so the medium changes nothing about the duty.

questions.stem: A member's marketing brochure states that CFA charterholders achieve better performance results. Under Standard VII(B), the statement is most likely:

options.A: of concern only for candidates.
options.B: prohibited by the standard.
options.C: acceptable if the track record supports it.

rationales.A: The prohibition reaches members, charterholders and candidates equally; the guidance names all three in the same sentence. Nothing in it presumes a charterholder's competency or performance claims to be supported merely because the charter has been awarded.
rationales.B: Statements referring to CFA Institute, the CFA designation, or candidacy for the CFA designation that overstate the competency of an individual, or that assert or imply that superior performance can be expected from someone with the CFA designation, are prohibited by the standard. 'CFA charterholders achieve better performance results' and 'As a CFA charterholder, Jane White provides the best value in trade execution' are both improper on that basis: each converts the designation into a forecast of results.
rationales.C: A track record cannot cure the defect, because the prohibited claim is that the designation itself produces superior performance. A member may state a factual accomplishment if it is true, but may not link it to the designation as evidence that superior results should be expected.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(B), a member's claim about the relative merits of CFA Institute, the CFA exams, or the Code and Standards is most likely:

options.A: permitted if stated as the speaker's opinion.
options.B: prohibited regardless of how it is framed.
options.C: permitted only with peer-reviewed support.

rationales.A: Members and candidates may make claims about the relative merits of CFA Institute, the CFA exams, or the Code and Standards as long as those statements are implicitly or explicitly stated as the opinion of the speaker. Statements that do not express opinions must be supported by facts. Framing each statement honestly, as opinion or as fact, and holding evidence behind the ones offered as fact, is the core compliance practice here.
rationales.B: Framing is what makes such a claim acceptable rather than what condemns it. A comparative claim is permitted when stated, implicitly or explicitly, as the opinion of the speaker, and equally permitted when offered as fact and supported by facts; only the unframed, unsupported assertion is improper.
rationales.C: No academic or peer-reviewed support is required. A relative-merit claim stated as the speaker's opinion stands as it is, and a claim presented as fact needs facts behind it rather than publication in a reviewed source. The requirement is honest framing, not citation.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(B), marketing material that refers to employees' CFA designations and exam results is most likely:

options.A: subject to review for factual accuracy.
options.B: subject to review only when client-facing.
options.C: exempt from review as firm opinion.

rationales.A: Marketing material referring to the designation must be reviewed for factual accuracy before use. Candidates do not receive their actual exam scores: topic and subtopic results are grouped into three broad categories and the exam is graded only pass or fail, so a candidate who sees a topical result above 70% cannot factually state that he received the highest possible score, because that information is not reported. Factual accomplishments may be stated where true, such as that all of a firm's principals passed the three exams on the first attempt, but they must not be linked to performance or imply superior ability. Firm-wide templates and a standing review process reduce both kinds of error.
rationales.B: The standard applies to any form of communication, so internal promotional drafts that refer to the designation require the same factual review as client-facing material. Limiting review to what reaches clients leaves the inaccuracy in place until the moment it is hardest to catch.
rationales.C: Marketing material is not exempt. It must be reviewed for factual accuracy, and labeling an unsupported performance claim as the firm's opinion does not make it permissible; a statement that does not express an opinion must be supported by facts, and a claim of superior performance from the designation is prohibited however it is framed.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(B), a charterholder who retires from the investment industry most likely:

options.A: may no longer use the designation.
options.B: may be reclassified as retired at reduced dues.
options.C: is reclassified as retired on ceasing full dues.

rationales.A: Retirement does not forfeit the designation. CFA Institute has procedures for reclassifying a member and charterholder as retired and reducing the annual dues, and use of the designation continues once that reclassification has been obtained, so the right is preserved rather than lost.
rationales.B: CFA Institute has procedures for reclassifying a member and charterholder as retired and reducing the annual dues. Retired status is not automatic: to obtain it, and to continue using the designation, the member must complete the appropriate process and meet the requirements for retired status established by CFA Institute.
rationales.C: Retired status is not conferred by lapsing into non-payment. The member must complete the appropriate process and meet the requirements for retired status established by CFA Institute; simply stopping payment of full dues leaves membership out of good standing rather than reclassified, and use of the designation is not supported in that condition.

questions.stem: Under Standard VII(B), the recommended role of a member's firm in securing accurate references to the CFA designation is most likely:

options.A: banning mention of the designation in firm materials.
options.B: leaving accuracy to the individual member.
options.C: creating firm-wide templates for such references.

rationales.A: Prohibition is not the aim. The objective is consistent and accurate reference to CFA Institute membership, the CFA designation and candidacy for the designation, and a blanket ban suppresses truthful disclosure that members are entitled to make instead of improving the accuracy of what is said.
rationales.B: The firm has a constructive role to play. Members and candidates should disseminate written information about Standard VII(B) and the accompanying guidance to their firm's legal, compliance, public relations and marketing departments, and should encourage the firm to create templates for materials that refer to employees' affiliation with CFA Institute.
rationales.C: Creating firm-wide templates consistent with Standard VII(B) promotes consistent and accurate references to CFA Institute membership, the CFA designation and candidacy for the designation. Combined with disseminating the guidance to the firm's legal, compliance, public relations and marketing departments, template use reduces both accidental exaggeration and improper implications of a partial designation or of an expected completion date.
